column3: The Hebrew reads “they surrounded him”; NASB has “turned aside,” as in 1 Kings 22:32. “Lured” is rendered “diverted.”
“From after him” is rendered “from pursuing him.”
“To his innocence” is rendered “at random,” and “between the joints and the body armor” as “in a joint of the armor.” “The camp” is rendered “the fight,” and NASB adds “severely.”
“Went up” is rendered “raged,” and “was holding upright” as “propped himself up.”
